verses.text: Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah to say, "May the gods punish me, and even more, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the life of one of those prophets!"
Elijah was afraid. He got up and ran for his life. He came to Beersheba in Judah and left his servant there.

Then he went on alone a whole day's walk into the desert. He came to a broom bush, sat down under it, and asked God to let him die. "I have had enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life. I am no better than my ancestors."
He lay down under the bush and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
He looked around, and there by his head was a loaf of bread baked on hot coals, and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and then lay down again.
The LORD's angel came back a second time, touched him, and said, "Get up and eat, because the journey ahead is too long for you."
So he got up, ate, and drank. That food gave him strength to walk forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he went into a cave and spent the night. Then the LORD's word came to him. The LORD said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He answered, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Armies. The Israelites have turned away from your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me too."

The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain in front of the LORD." Then the LORD passed by. A great and powerful wind tore the mountains apart and broke the rocks into pieces in front of the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire there was a quiet, gentle whisper.
When Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his cloak, went out, and stood at the entrance of the cave. Then a voice said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He answered, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Armies. The Israelites have turned away from your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me too."
The LORD said to him, "Go back the way you came, and go to the desert of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.
Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king over Israel. And anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel Meholah, to be prophet in your place.
Jehu will kill anyone who escapes the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will kill anyone who escapes the sword of Jehu.
But I have kept seven thousand people in Israel for myself. They have not bowed down to Baal, and they have not kissed his idol."
So Elijah left there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve pairs of oxen ahead of him, and he was driving the twelfth pair. Elijah went over to him and threw his cloak over him.
Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, "Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you." Elijah said, "Go on back. What have I done to stop you?"

So Elisha went back. He took his pair of oxen and killed them. He used the wooden plowing gear to cook the meat, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up, followed Elijah, and became his helper.
